questiontext.text:
Drag the correct syntax element into the blanks to declare a PHP array.

$fruits = [[1]] "apple", "banana", "cherry" [[2]];

correctfeedback.text: Correct! Arrays in PHP are enclosed in square brackets.

partiallycorrectfeedback.text: Check the array syntax in PHP.

incorrectfeedback.text: PHP arrays use square brackets [ ] to enclose elements.

questiontext.text:
Drag the correct keywords into the blanks to complete a foreach loop.

[[1]] ($array [[2]] $item) {
    echo $item;
}

correctfeedback.text: Correct! foreach iterates over array elements.

incorrectfeedback.text: The correct syntax is: foreach ($array as $item)

name.text: PHP Image Equivalent 01 - String method identification

questiontext.text:
Image-equivalent task: Study the diagram below and identify the marked component.

In the code snippet, identify the name of the string method indicated by the box labeled COMPONENT A:

$text = "Hello World";
        ╔══════════╗
        ║ COMPONENT A
        ║ (method name)
        ║
$result = $text->strtolower();
         ▲
         └─ This is where it's applied

Type the exact method name (without parentheses or object reference):

feedback.text: Correct! strtolower() converts a string to lowercase. In PHP, this is typically used as str_replace() or similar, but in this object-oriented context, we use strtolower().
Also acceptable - this is the common naming convention, though PHP uses strtolower().

name.text: PHP Image Equivalent 02 - Conditional operator symbol

questiontext.text:
Image-equivalent task: Identify the marked operator in the diagram below.

In the ternary expression, type the operator symbol indicated by BOX B:

$status = (age > 18) BOX_B "Adult" : "Minor";
                    ▲
                    │
                   BOX B
           (comparison operator)

This operator checks whether the value is greater than a threshold.

Type only the operator symbol:

feedback.text: Correct! The ? operator starts the true branch of a ternary conditional. The full syntax is: condition ? true_value : false_value
